name: Nahum
whenBasis: He speaks of Thebes' fall as past (Nahum 3:8), which Assyria sacked in 663 BC, and of Nineveh's as coming, which fell in 612 BC.
summary: Nahum the Elkoshite, whose book is a single burden against Nineveh, the capital of Assyria. The LORD is slow to anger but will not leave the guilty unpunished; Nineveh, the city of blood, will be flooded, plundered and laid waste, and no one will grieve for her. For Judah, it is good news: the feet of one who brings it are on the mountains.
body: He asks Nineveh whether it is better than Thebes, stationed by the Nile, which also went into exile. In Jonah, Nineveh repents and is spared.

later.text: A Babylonian chronicle records that the Medes and Babylonians took Nineveh in 612 BC.

sources.title: Babylonian Chronicle of the fall of Nineveh, British Museum 21901
